li: preposition; Allah: genitive after it. The phrase is the predicate (khabar) of al-ḥamd.
Adjective (naʿt) of 'Allah', genitive; also muḍāf.

wa: conjunction. iyyāka: object brought forward, accusative position.

Substitute (badal) for al-ṣirāṭ, so accusative; also muḍāf.
Relative noun (ism mawṣūl), fixed (mabnī) on fatḥah, in the genitive position as muḍāf ilayh.
Past-tense verb; tu: the subject pronoun 'you'. The sentence is the ṣilah of alladhīna.
ʿalā: preposition; him: pronoun in the genitive position. Linked to 'anʿamta'.
Substitute (badal) or adjective of alladhīna, genitive; also muḍāf.

wa: conjunction; lā: particle stressing the negation.

wa: conjunction; lam: jazm particle; yūlad: passive present verb, jussive; sign: sukūn.
lam: jazm particle; yakun: incomplete verb (kāna and its sisters), jussive; sign: sukūn.
li: preposition; hu: pronoun, genitive. Linked to kufuwan.

Noun of yakun (ism yakun) placed last, nominative; sign: ḍammah with tanwīn.
inna: particle of emphasis that makes its noun accusative; nā: its noun, in the accusative position.
Past verb; nā: subject; ka: first object. The sentence is the predicate of inna.

fa: particle of consequence; ṣalli: verb of command built on dropping the final yāʾ; subject: hidden 'you'.
li: preposition; rabbi: genitive and muḍāf; ka: muḍāf ilayh.
wa: conjunction; inḥar: verb of command, fixed on sukūn.

Predicate of inna, nominative; sign: ḍammah.
wa: particle of oath (ḥarf qasam), a preposition; al-ʿaṣr: genitive after it; sign: kasrah.

Noun of inna, accusative; sign: fatḥah.

wa: conjunction; ʿamilū: past verb, the wāw is its subject.
